name: Dunkirk
title: Dunkirk Ship Thickness Measurement & Drydock UTM
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging in Dunkirk (Dunkerque): drydock UTM at the repair yard, ferry refits, bulk carrier ESP surveys and SECA scrubber piping.
h1: Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Dunkirk (Dunkerque)
intro: Dunkirk combines a deep-water western port, with ore and coal carriers, container ships, LNG carriers and the Dover Strait ferries, and an eastern port behind locks with older basins and lay-by berths. The dry docks and floating dock of Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque give ships a docking option at the eastern end of the Channel, which is why superintendents ask us for in-dock gauging here as well as readings during calls. We mobilise a team from India to Dunkirk, timed to the docking or the call.

highlights.p: The dry docks and floating dock of Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque sit close to the Dover Strait. Gauging planned into the yard stay lets steel renewal be cut and fitted before the ship undocks.

highlights.h: Ore and coal carrier ESP work
highlights.p: Large bulk carriers discharging ore and coal for the steelworks carry the grab damage and cargo-related corrosion that ESP renewal surveys examine. Ballast tanks can be gauged during discharge and holds once they are clear.
A refit is when a ro-pax ferry's vehicle decks, ramps and tanks can be reached. Scrubber pipe inspection in Dunkirk is worth adding for ferries that run inside the SECA all year.

port.h: The port of Dunkirk and its shipping
p: Dunkirk (Dunkerque) is run by the Grand Port Maritime de Dunkerque and stretches along the French North Sea coast near the Belgian border, at the eastern end of the Dover Strait. The port has two distinct halves. The western port at Loon-Plage is the deep-water side, with the container terminal, the ore and coal quays that feed the integrated steelworks, the Dunkerque LNG terminal and the ferry terminal for the Dover services. The eastern port, reached through locks, holds the older basins with general cargo, bulk, lay-by and repair berths. The two halves are linked by road along the coast and run by the same port authority.

The traffic mix is heavy and industrial. Large bulk carriers bring iron ore and coal for the steel plant, LNG carriers discharge at the Dunkerque LNG terminal, and container ships, ro-ro ships and car carriers call at the western terminals. The Dover–Dunkirk ro-pax ferries run frequent daily crossings of the strait, and the port also handles tankers, short-sea traders, and the dredgers and service craft that keep the approach channels open along this shallow, sandbank-lined coast.

What sets Dunkirk apart on the French side of the Channel is docking capacity. Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque operates dry docks and a floating dock in the port, and its work covers oceangoing and offshore vessels as well as ferries, ro-ro and ro-pax ships and dredgers, with ferry operators among its regular customers. That gives two kinds of gauging window. One is the planned docking, where tanks, shell and internal structure are opened up for the yard. The other is the bulk carrier or LNG carrier alongside for a discharge, where ballast tanks and deck structure can be gauged during the berth time. Ships also lay by in the eastern basins between employment, which suits pre-purchase or condition gauging that needs several uninterrupted days on board.

facilities.h: Gauging locations in the western and eastern ports
p: For drydock gauging in Dunkirk, the Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque docks are the centre of activity. A ship in dock gives full access to the bottom and side shell, sea chests and the internal structure of tanks once they are cleaned and ventilated, and the readings can be turned round quickly enough for the yard to cut and renew steel within the same stay. The yard's dry docks and floating dock between them cover ferries, dredgers, offshore vessels and oceangoing cargo ships.

In the western port, gauging is fitted around cargo work. Ore and coal carriers discharge with grabs in the holds, so the team works in the hopper, topside and double-bottom ballast tanks while discharge continues and reaches each hold only once it is cleared. LNG carriers at the terminal are subject to its gas-safety rules, and container ships follow the usual short-call pattern of ballast tanks and deck structure first. The Dover Strait traffic separation scheme is on the doorstep, so a ship transiting the strait can divert into Dunkirk for a docking or a gauging call with little deviation from its route.
list: Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque dry docks — renewal-survey and docking gauging of bottom, side shell, tanks and internal structure while the ship is in dock.
Damen floating dock — refit-period gauging on ferries, dredgers, offshore vessels and smaller cargo ships, including vehicle decks, ramps and sea chests.
Western port ore and coal quays — hopper, topside and double-bottom tank gauging on large bulk carriers during discharge, with holds gauged once clear.
Dunkerque LNG terminal, Loon-Plage — ballast-tank and hull structure gauging on LNG carriers within the terminal's safety rules.
Western port container and ro-ro terminals — short-call gauging of ballast tanks, deck structure and scrubber piping on container ships and car carriers.
Eastern port basins behind the locks — lay-by gauging for pre-purchase, off-hire or condition surveys that need several days of uninterrupted access.

context.h: Port state control, SECA and the steel-and-energy trades at Dunkirk
p: Dunkirk lies inside the North Sea SOx ECA, at the narrow eastern end of the Channel, and France applies port state control under the Paris MoU. The Dover Strait is among the busiest shipping lanes in the world, and the ships using Dunkirk's western port tend to be large and hard-worked: bulk carriers in the ore and coal trades, whose holds and hopper tanks see grab damage and the corrosion that wet coal cargoes promote, and LNG carriers on regular European discharge rotations. Both are ship types on which port state control inspectors look closely for wastage and cracking at structural details.

Bulk carriers are ESP ships. Under SOLAS chapter XI-1 regulation 2 and IACS UR Z10.2 or Z10.5, the third renewal survey at about 15 years and later surveys bring extensive gauging of holds, hopper and topside tanks and transverse bulkheads, which is where measured readings taken during an earlier discharge pay off. Ferries and container ships are surveyed under UR Z7 and their society's rules. The EU ETS (since 2024) and FuelEU Maritime (since 2025) apply to every call, and the cross-Channel ferries show the SECA's effect on piping most clearly: a scrubber-fitted ferry that never leaves the ECA runs its wash-water system on every crossing.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Dunkirk
jobs.p: Dunkirk work falls into docking jobs, where the yard's programme sets the pace, and berth jobs, where discharge time does. A single Schengen visa covers France and neighbouring Belgium, so a Dunkirk docking can share a trip with a call at Zeebrugge, Ghent or Antwerp when an owner has ships in both. Bulk carrier thickness measurement and ferry work dominate:
list: Renewal-survey gauging on a ro-pax ferry during a refit at Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque, covering vehicle decks, ramps, ballast and fuel tanks and the shell plating around the waterline.
Third renewal survey gauging on a Capesize bulk carrier: hopper and topside tanks during ore discharge in the western port, then holds and transverse bulkheads once the holds are cleaned.
Pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks on an LNG carrier at the Dunkerque LNG terminal, so steel and coating repairs can be specified before the ship goes to its next yard.
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a general cargo ship laid by in the eastern basins, giving the buyer measured plate thickness for the sale decision.
Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping gauging on a container ship or car carrier at the western terminals, timed to the cargo window.

logistics: The usual routes are Paris Charles de Gaulle with rail connections north through Lille, or Brussels Airport with an onward road transfer along the coast. The ship's agent requests ISPS passes for the named technicians at the western port terminals, and yard access for a docking is arranged with Damen Shiprepair Dunkerque. Each technician travels on a Schengen visa applied for in India once the docking slot or berth date is firm; an invitation letter from the owner or yard naming the vessel supports the application. Because yard slots can move, flights are confirmed against the yard's latest schedule rather than the original booking.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a cross-Channel ferry during its refit at Dunkirk?
faqs.a: Yes. A refit gives access to the spaces that cannot be reached in service: vehicle-deck plating under lashing points, ramp structure, ballast and fuel tanks, and the shell where it is exposed in dock. We plan the gauging with the refit manager so tanks are measured as soon as they are opened, and report by area so the yard can renew steel before the ferry returns to service.

faqs.q: Do you work in the eastern port as well as the deep-water western port?
faqs.a: Yes. The two halves of the port are connected by road and the agent arranges access to both. The western port is where the large bulk carriers, LNG carriers and container ships berth; the eastern port, behind the locks, has lay-by berths that suit longer, uninterrupted gauging. Lock transits are planned by the ship and the port, so we time boarding to the ship's movement.

faqs.q: Can one mobilisation cover a docking in Dunkirk and a ship in a Belgian port?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. France and Belgium are both Schengen states, so the same visa covers Dunkirk and the Belgian ports a short drive along the coast. If an owner has a docking at Dunkirk and a ship calling at Zeebrugge, Ghent or Antwerp in the same period, we can plan one trip and sequence the jobs around the docking dates and the second ship's berth window.

faqs.q: How much notice does a Dunkirk docking need?
faqs.a: As much as the docking itself allows. Dockings are planned months ahead, and that is the time to involve us: the Schengen visa application, the TM plan and the team size all depend on the docking date and the expected scope. If the date slips, the travel moves with it; if the yard brings the ship in early, an issued visa and an agreed plan are what let the team follow.
